key_insight: Deep-learning emulators can replace a costly marine biogeochemistry model while staying stable over days to decades and preserving forecast skill.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path to faster, higher-quality ocean ecosystem forecasting for climate studies, operational prediction, and autonomous systems.
method: LSTM emulators predict selected daily variables in a one-dimensional water-column model.
Physics-informed 1D CNNs emulate the full pelagic system throughout the water column at daily resolution.
Models are driven by ocean physics simulator inputs and compared against the parent model in short-range and multi-decadal tests.
evidence_signal: The emulators were evaluated on daily variability, extreme events, 10-day forecasts, and decadal climate projections, and when trained on reanalysis data they outperformed the parent model for key ecosystem variables.
watch_item: Performance is shown in a simplified one-dimensional framework, so scaling to full three-dimensional regional oceans may require substantial retraining and careful validation.
paper_title: Deep learning model emulators for marine biogeochemistry forecasting from days to decades
